root_idea.summary: The root centers on self-restraint: a condition or practice by which desire is held in check, especially through abstinence and chastity.
root_idea.development: The Quran-focused evidence connects seeking عفّة with practicing restraint and relates the idea to taking only a little or to a remainder. Classical evidence also preserves specialized branches involving residual milk and selectively taking what remains or what is best.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form X perfect citation form.
Displayed as the Quran-attested Form V verbal noun.

senses.definition: To seek abstinence; to restrain oneself from what is unlawful or from overpowering desire, and thus preserve chastity.
senses.usage_conditions: A self-directed Form X construction, used with an expressed object or with عن, and often leaving the object implicit. The Quranic occurrences apply this self-restraint in contexts including the handling of dependent wealth and maintaining chastity when marriage is unavailable.

senses.definition: Self-restraint, abstinence, or chastity: the cultivated state or practice of holding desire in check.
senses.usage_conditions: A Form V verbal noun denoting the state or practice of restraint rather than a single act. In the Quranic occurrence it describes the restraint of people whose need is not readily apparent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abstain or refrain from an unlawful, unseemly, indecorous, or otherwise inviolable thing; to be abstinent, continent, chaste, modest, or decorous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I. The object may be left unexpressed or introduced with عن; عفَّ عن المسألة specifically means to refrain from begging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of milk, to collect in the udder or to remain there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said specifically of milk in the udder; the lexical reports distinguish newly collected milk from milk remaining after most has been taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seeking abstinence, including refraining from begging or asking people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical extension of the Form X verbal noun; the construction may combine abstention from unlawful things with abstention from begging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone to drink عُفَافَة, the milk left in an udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II, transitive; the object supplied as drink is the residual milk called عُفَافَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone abstinent or chaste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative usage, as in making a person عفيف.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe or she-goat, to have milk collected or remaining in the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV usage said of a ewe or she-goat and connected with the milk sense of عُفَافَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drink عُفَافَة, the residual milk left in an udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage with a person as subject and residual milk as the consumed object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To milk one's camel after the first milking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI construction used with a camel as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat oneself medically or seek medical treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI reflexive usage; it may occur in the question بِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ نَتَعَافُّ, “With what shall we treat ourselves medically?”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to lick up or take the choicest dry herbage from above the ground or dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII usage describing selective taking of dry herbage with the tongue.
A separate nominal usage reported as a substituted form related to عُثَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain small, smooth, white fish, said when cooked to taste like rice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for the fish described in the lexical evidence.
A specialized nominal usage distinct from the abstinence sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abstinent, continent, chaste, virtuous, modest, decent, or decorous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective derived from the abstinence sense; its feminine form is عَفِيفَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Excellent, high-born, good, righteous, or virtuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine adjective applied to a woman; the same form is also commonly used in the sense “chaste,” which belongs to the preceding adjectival branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The milk collected in an udder, or the milk remaining there after most has been sucked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun derived from the milk usage of عَفَّ; the evidence reports both a collected-milk and a residual-milk interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What is taken piece by piece from the ground by licking or similar means, especially the choicest portion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized interpretation attributed in the lexical discussion; the explanation may refer to the thing taken rather than to the act of taking it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression جاء على عِفَّانِ ذلك, at the time of that.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or substituted form used in a fixed temporal expression.
